dates.notes: Signed by New Zealand, Chile and Singapore on 11 June 2020 GMT (12 June 2020 New Zealand time). Entered into force for New Zealand and Singapore on 7 January 2021 and for Chile on 23 November 2021. Korea's accession took effect on 3 May 2024. Costa Rica presented its Instrument of Accession on 17 September 2026; the joint press release does not state the date on which the Agreement enters into force for Costa Rica. A Protocol to the DEPA was signed on 15 July 2023; sources differ between 19 and 20 March 2024 for its entry into force.

legal_nature.rationale: A treaty with final provisions, a depositary (Article 16.1), entry into force on notification by the Parties (Article 16.2) and accession (Article 16.4). The AI provision is hortatory but sits inside a binding agreement.

ai_provisions: Article 8.2 — Artificial Intelligence: recognition of AI's economic and social importance; promotion of ethical and governance frameworks; consideration of internationally recognised principles including explainability, transparency, fairness and human-centred values
relevance.excluded_scope: The AI article does not create enforceable substantive standards, conformity assessment or market-access conditions; it commits the Parties to promote and endeavour.
relevance.reason: A binding digital-economy agreement whose Module 8 contains a dedicated article on artificial intelligence. The AI provision is expressly included in a treaty, although its operative language is cooperative and best-efforts ('shall endeavour'), not a set of prohibitions or product rules.

status_note: In force for New Zealand, Singapore, Chile and Korea. Costa Rica became the fifth Party on presenting its Instrument of Accession in Auckland on 17 September 2026, the second State to accede after Korea. The joint press release announces the accession but does not state an entry-into-force date for Costa Rica; the depositary notification was not read, so that date is recorded as unknown.
